baslik: The Rocket Shut Down on the Pad and the Pilot Didn't Eject
sonuc: had its engines shut down on the pad
tetik: a plug that fell out early and a dust cover left inside the engine
mekanizma: a forgotten plastic dust cover blocking oxidizer flow in the gas generator
ders: launch plugs were replaced and assembly checks tightened
yanilgi: The shutdown wasn't just a loose plug. A dust cover had been left inside the engine months earlier.
tartisma: The commander trusted his senses over the clock and didn't eject. Was it courage or luck?
basliklar: Why Gemini 6A Shut Down on the Pad
The Dust Cover Left Inside a Rocket
sahneler: Gemini 6A's engines ignited, then suddenly shut down on the pad.
The mission clock started, signalling lift-off, but the rocket hadn't moved.
Rules said the crew should eject.
Wally Schirra felt no movement and decided not to.
An electrical plug had dropped out early.
But thrust had already been decaying.
A plastic dust cover had been left inside the engine.
It had blocked the flow of oxidizer.

baslik: A Wire Rubbing on a Screw Nearly Downed a Shuttle
sonuc: lost engine controllers seconds after launch
tetik: a wire chafed against an exposed screw head

tartisma: Redundancy saved the flight by a narrow margin. How thin was the margin?

The Wire That Almost Ended a Shuttle Flight
sahneler: Columbia lifted off carrying the Chandra X-ray Observatory.
Seconds later, an electrical short suddenly knocked out two engine controllers.
Backup controllers kept the engines running.
A wire had been rubbing on an exposed screw head.
At the same time, a gold pin shot out inside an engine.
It caused a hydrogen leak.
The shuttle still reached orbit.
Every orbiter's wiring was then inspected.

baslik: The Mars Lander That Kept Rebooting Itself
sonuc: kept resetting its computer on Mars
tetik: priority inversion under heavy load
mekanizma: a low-priority task holding a resource needed by a high-priority task, triggering resets
ders: engineers patched the software from Earth to enable priority inheritance
yanilgi: The bug wasn't unknown. It had shown up in testing and was judged a minor glitch.
tartisma: It was fixed from millions of kilometres away. What makes a remote fix possible?
basliklar: Why Mars Pathfinder Kept Rebooting
The Priority Inversion on Mars
soru: What makes a remote fix possible?
sahneler: Days after landing on Mars, NASA's Pathfinder lander started rebooting.
Suddenly its computer reset, halting operations until the next day.
The bug had appeared in testing before launch.
It was judged a rare glitch and given low priority.
A low-priority task was blocking a high-priority one.
It's called priority inversion.
Engineers reproduced it on a duplicate on Earth.
They patched the software on Mars.

baslik: The Solar Wing That Bent Itself to Pieces
sonuc: broke up and fell into the Pacific
tetik: turbulence bending the wing into a high dihedral shape
mekanizma: a flexible wing morphing into a persistent high dihedral, leading to unstable oscillations
ders: the mishap report pushed better modelling of flexible aircraft

The Wing That Bent Too Far
sahneler: NASA's solar-powered Helios broke apart over the Pacific.
Within minutes of hitting turbulence, it fell into the ocean.
It was a huge, light flying wing.
A delayed take-off kept it climbing slowly through rough air.
Turbulence bent the wing sharply upward.
It stayed bent.
Its pitch swings grew with every cycle until it broke.
The report called for better modelling of flexible aircraft.

baslik: Faulty Sensors Shut Down a Shuttle Engine in Flight
sonuc: lost an engine during launch
tetik: two temperature sensors failing in turn
mekanizma: faulty sensor readings triggering an automatic engine shutdown
ders: sensor logic was reviewed and the mission still completed its work

The Only Shuttle Abort After Launch

Suddenly the crew had to perform an abort to orbit.
A temperature sensor on the engine failed.
Two minutes later, a second one failed.
The computer shut the engine down.
The engine itself was fine.
A flight controller had further automatic shutdowns blocked.
It remains the only shuttle abort after launch.

baslik: The Autonomous Spacecraft That Bumped Into Its Target
sonuc: collided with the satellite it was meant to approach
tetik: a navigation failure at close range
mekanizma: inaccurate position data feeding a collision-avoidance system that then failed
ders: NASA's review fed lessons into later autonomous rendezvous work
yanilgi: Nobody was flying it. The spacecraft trusted its own bad numbers.

basliklar: Why NASA's DART Crashed Into Its Target
The Robot That Misjudged the Distance
sahneler: A NASA spacecraft built to approach another satellite on its own collided with it.
Suddenly the mission ended, far short of its goals.
Its navigation had failed at close range.
A precision sensor never fully switched on.
The craft kept approaching with inaccurate data.
Its collision-avoidance system relied on the same bad data.
It burned through propellant faster than expected.
The review shaped later autonomous rendezvous work.

baslik: The Hypersonic Test That Failed in 13 Seconds
sonuc: was destroyed after its booster lost control
tetik: a control oscillation in the booster at transonic speed
mekanizma: inaccurate modelling producing an inadequate control system that let an elevon fail
ders: better modelling led to record-setting later flights
yanilgi: No single part was to blame. Many small modelling errors added up.
tartisma: The next flights set speed records. Is failure the fastest teacher?

The Booster That Lost Control
sahneler: A B-52 released the X-43A and its booster rocket.
Within seconds, the booster began to oscillate and lost control.
About thirteen seconds after release, it deviated from its course.
An elevon on the rocket failed.
It was destroyed for safety.
Investigators found many small modelling errors.
Together they produced an inadequate control system.
Later flights set speed records.

baslik: A Photo Shoot That Destroyed a Supersonic Bomber

mekanizma: a chase fighter drifting into the bomber in tight formation
ders: the crash raised questions about publicity flights with test aircraft

The Formation Flight That Went Wrong
sahneler: In a photo formation, an F-104 fighter collided with the giant XB-70 bomber.
Both aircraft crashed, and two pilots were killed.
Five jets were flying in close formation.
They were being photographed for their engine maker.
The F-104 drifted into the bomber's wing.
It rolled over the XB-70 and exploded.
The Valkyrie lost its tail and crashed.
Only one XB-70 remains, in a museum.

baslik: A Lit Flare Thrown Into a Locker Full of Flares

tetik: a lit flare locked inside a flare locker
mekanizma: an accidentally ignited flare setting off hundreds of flares in a sealed locker
ders: the fire became a lesson in ordnance handling on carriers

The Flare Locked Inside a Locker
soru: How do you fight what you can't reach?
sahneler: Fire broke out on the carrier Oriskany off Vietnam.

A flare had been accidentally ignited.
The sailor holding it threw it into a flare locker.
He sealed the door.
The other flares were about to ignite.
Pressure made the locker door impossible to open.
Within five minutes, the locker exploded.

baslik: A Destroyer Full of Radar Didn't See a Container Ship

tetik: a bridge team that lost situational awareness
mekanizma: late recognition of a crossing ship and orders that were not carried out
ders: the Navy overhauled training and readiness in its Pacific fleet

The Warship That Didn't See It Coming

The destroyer carried advanced radar.
The bridge team lost track of the ships around them.
An order to turn and speed up came late.
It wasn't carried out in time.
Officers faced court proceedings.
The Navy overhauled training in its Pacific fleet.

baslik: The Touchscreen Steering That Confused a Warship's Crew

mekanizma: overly complex touchscreen controls and a fatigued crew mishandling a steering transfer

The Touchscreen That Steered a Ship Into a Tanker

The crew believed they'd lost steering.
Control had been shifted between stations.
The touchscreen controls were overly complex.
Sailors weren't sure where key indicators were.
Reports also cited fatigue and poor communication.
The Navy moved back toward physical controls.

The Chart That Moved a Reef

Within days it was declared lost, and it was later cut apart on the reef.
The crew used a digital chart.
It placed the reef miles from its real position.
Other charts showed it correctly.
The crew didn't cross-check them.
Investigators called the grounding preventable.
The ship was dismantled on the reef.

baslik: A Submarine Hit an Undersea Mountain at Full Speed

tetik: a seamount missing from the chart in use

yanilgi: The mountain wasn't completely unknown. Other charts hinted at it.

The Seamount Missing From the Chart
sahneler: Deep underwater near Guam, a nuclear submarine hit a mountain.
Suddenly the crew was thrown forward, and one sailor later died.
It was running at flank speed.
The seamount wasn't on the chart in use.
Other charts showed signs of it.
That warning hadn't been transferred.

The Navy reviewed how chart hazards are shared.

baslik: A Warship Burned for Four Days in Port

tetik: a fire on a lower vehicle deck during maintenance
mekanizma: a fire in a ship under maintenance spreading while defenses were degraded
ders: the Navy scrapped the ship and reviewed fire readiness in port

sahneler: A fire started on a US Navy assault ship docked in San Diego.
It spread for days, and dozens of sailors and civilians were injured.
The ship was undergoing maintenance.
The fire began on a lower vehicle deck.
It took four days to put out.
Repairs would have cost billions.
The ship was scrapped instead.
A sailor charged with arson was acquitted.

mekanizma: vaporized lubricating oil from a hydraulic catapult igniting below decks

The Catapult That Blew Up a Carrier
sahneler: Explosions ripped through the carrier Bennington off Rhode Island.
Within seconds, fire swept below decks, and one hundred three men were killed.
The ship used hydraulic catapults to launch aircraft.
A catapult accumulator burst.
It released vaporized lubricating oil.
The vapour ignited.
An inquiry found the hazard had been known.
The Navy switched to steam catapults.

tetik: a night collision with USS John F. Kennedy

sahneler: Off Sicily at night, the cruiser Belknap collided with the carrier John F. Kennedy.

Seven died on Belknap and one on the carrier.
The cruiser's superstructure was aluminum.
It saved weight.
But heat weakened it quickly.
The superstructure collapsed in the fire.
The Navy moved back toward steel.

It performed an emergency surfacing manoeuvre for them.

The visitor program came under intense scrutiny.

soru: What matters in the first minute?

Training after an earlier carrier fire helped limit the damage.

sahneler: A B-52 carrying two nuclear bombs broke apart over North Carolina.
Suddenly both bombs fell toward the ground.

The bomber lost structural integrity.

Some safety devices on one bomb activated during the fall.

It pushed improvements in weapon safety design.
